summary: A cast-iron tower at Woods Hole, lit since 1828 and rebuilt in 1876; its keepers, its 1935 rescue, and the Friends who have owned it since 2025.

access.note: Tower visited on scheduled tours run by the Friends of Nobska Light; the 2026 season was closed when checked on 2026-10-22; private tours on request.

facts.agency: Friends of Nobska Light, Inc. (owner since the 21 July 2025 deed from the U.S. Coast Guard)

events.note: Light built on top of the keeper's dwelling (NRHP form; LighthouseFriends gives 1828 and $2,949.30). USLHS record gives 1829 as year established
First light shown from the keeper's dwelling roof; year conflicts with USLHS 1829
Fifth-order lens installed in the original light (LighthouseFriends)
Fog bell sounded by machinery (LighthouseFriends)
Lighthouse Board finds the station dilapidated and says it needs rebuilding (as LighthouseFriends reports)
Cast-iron tower lined with brick and wood-frame dwelling erected; the 1981 form dates the complex mainly to 1876
USLHS record gives 1876 as the year the original (fourth-order) lens was installed; LighthouseFriends says a fifth-order lens moved to the new tower in 1876
Brick oil house and paint lockers; new keeper's dwelling (wood)
Fourth-order lens with red sector placed in December 1887 (LighthouseFriends); conflicts with USLHS 1876
Stone wall five feet thick built to protect the bell tower site (report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1892; the month within July 1891 to June 1892 is not given)
Covered way from dwelling to tower built; cistern built (report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1899)
New house for the fog bell's striking machine; bell tower strengthened (report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1900)

Second keeper's house built to the south (1981 form). LighthouseFriends mentions a second dwelling added for George Cameron when he became first assistant (roster dates that appointment to 1910); the sources do not reconcile the dates
First-class Daboll trumpet goes into operation on the point after a dispute with summer residents
George I. Cameron becomes head keeper after the death of Oliver A. Nickerson
Boston-bound steamer Bunker Hill ran aground on a clear, calm night in an area LighthouseFriends calls hazardous; all passengers unloaded safely (LighthouseFriends only; no newspaper was read)
Keepers in the second and third districts, Nobska Point among them, to submit data on the 24 January 1925 eclipse of the sun
Keeper John M. Scharff and assistant keeper Waldo Leighton rescue a man thrown from a sailboat in a windstorm (August 1935)
125-foot steel radiobeacon tower and radiobeacon building (LighthouseFriends and USLHS say 1937; the 1981 form dates the steel tower to 1948)
Light automated and unmanned; living quarters used by the Woods Hole Coast Guard group commander
Coast Guard license to the Town of Falmouth as steward; formal transfer 25 April 2016
Friends of Nobska Light open the restored tower and keeper's dwelling to the public
Deed received by Friends of Nobska Light from the U.S. Coast Guard, 21 July 2025

corrections.why: The 1828 light stood on the keeper's dwelling; the cast-iron tower the record describes was erected in 1876.
USLHS gives 40 feet from base to centre of lantern (about 12.2 m).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1828 light was set on the roof of the keeper's dwelling and was not a cast-iron tower; the iron tower the record describes was built in 1876 (NRHP form, LighthouseFriends and the USLHS record agree on 1876).

The NRHP form gives the land purchase and the light built on the keeper's dwelling as 7/7/1828 (LighthouseFriends also gives 1828); the USLHS record gives 1829 as 'Year Established'. The story gives both.

The USLHS record still gives the U.S. Coast Guard as owner, licensed to the Friends; the Friends' website says they received the deed on 21 July 2025. The story says the Friends own the station and notes the Society's older entry.

notes_for_editor: 1) First light year: 1828 (NRHP form land and building entries; LighthouseFriends) against 1829 (USLHS record 'Year Established'). Story says 1828 and notes the difference. 2) Brief lists a tower built 1831 and another built 1837; no source we read supports either, so neither is in the record. 3) Lens: USLHS says the original optic was a fourth-order Fresnel installed in 1876; LighthouseFriends says a fifth-order lens went into the old light in 1856, moved to the new tower in 1876, and was replaced by a fourth-order in December 1887; the 1981 form describes a fourth-order lens without a date. Unresolved. 4) Second keeper's house: 1900 (1981 form) against about 1910 (LighthouseFriends, when Cameron was appointed). Unresolved. 5) Steel radiobeacon tower: 1937 (LighthouseFriends; brief) against 1948 (1981 form). Unresolved. 6) Joseph G. Hindley: roster has him as first assistant 1956-1973 and Donald W. Selfe as head keeper 1967-1969; LighthouseFriends has Hindley as head keeper from 1968 to his retirement on 3 November 1972. Both are recorded; the story says so. 7) Roster matched to place by name and position (0.17 km). 8) Atmosphere: every scene detail comes from LighthouseFriends, the NRHP form, the Lighthouse Board volumes or the Bulletin. No general period context is used. 9) Chronicling America search for Nobska in Massachusetts papers, 1870-1915, and a second search for Bunker Hill (1911) both failed: loc.gov returned HTTP 520 on retries. The Bunker Hill grounding rests on LighthouseFriends alone. Its reference list names a Boston Daily Globe item of 24 October 1911, which concerns Cameron's family rather than the wreck; the Globe was not checked. 10) The Lighthouse Board annual reports in the local corpus start in 1891, so the 1828-1890 history rests on the NRHP form and LighthouseFriends. 11) Wikipedia was used only to find leads and is not cited. 12) Access: the Friends' page, read on 2026-10-22, says the 2026 public tour season is closed; check before a visit. 13) Post-1960 keepers are named only as the USLHS roster prints them (public role), with no personal details. 14) Coordinates in the brief (OSM) sit about 40 m from the NRHP form's coordinates; no correction proposed. 15) Characteristic: the 1981 form's OCR reads 'FIW, 6 sec.' with 'Red Sector'; the brief's 'Fl W 6s' is recorded on that reading (medium). Fog signal on the 1981 form: 'Horn 2/30 sec.' 16) Fact-check pass 2026-10-22: the opening now states the 1829 USLHS year beside 1828; the 1892, 1899 and 1900 Light-House Board citations are labelled by fiscal year (the volumes read say 'fiscal year ended June 30'). The Bunker Hill passenger remark (did not come within 100 feet of the light) is quoted by LighthouseFriends and is in the story. 17) The NRHP form dated 1981 carries a 1985 entry (automation and group commander quarters); the story cites it for that entry. 18) The Friends' own website (read 2026-10-22) gives the 2026 schedule: tours Tuesdays to Thursdays from 10 AM to 1 PM, June 2 to October 6, with Wednesday twilight tours from 5:30 PM, June 17 to September 2; the season is closed.
